description:
Sky Grid turns your morning into one small, honest ritual: step outside, capture the sky, and let the day begin.

No filters. No feed to scroll. No pressure to look good — just the true average color of the sky you actually saw, turned into one square in a mosaic that grows across the whole year.

HOW IT WORKS
- Open Sky Grid and your camera is already ready
- Capture the sky, once a day
- Watch today's color take its place in this year's 365-square Sky Grid
- Invite one trusted buddy — their morning stays blurred until you've shown up for yours too

WHY IT'S DIFFERENT
Most habit apps guilt you into showing up every single day. Sky Grid doesn't. Miss a morning and it simply waits for tomorrow's sky — your rhythm is measured by the week, not by a streak you're afraid to break. Every post is timestamped with when you captured it and when you posted it, so the record stays honest without needing to be strict.

WHAT'S FREE, ALWAYS
- Unlimited daily captures, posts, and buddies
- Your most recent 30 days in the Sky Grid archive
- Every core feature of the app — capture, grid, buddies, notifications

SKY GRID PRO
- The full, all-time Sky Grid archive
- Original-quality photo storage
- A yearly time-lapse export of your whole year
- Additional share card designs

Sky Grid was built around one idea: the sky looks a little different every single morning, and noticing it — just once a day — is worth keeping.

Terms of Use: https://skygrid.my/terms

promotionalText: Wake up, step outside, and capture the sky. No filters, no feed to scroll — just a quiet daily ritual that slowly becomes a year you can see.
whatsNew: Sky Grid now shows your actual morning photos, not just the extracted color, across your buddy strip and this week rhythm. Also includes: a gentle notification when your buddy captures their morning sky, with notification permission requested right when you connect with a buddy rather than only when you turn on the morning alarm, and an occasional reminder for solo mornings (no buddy yet) to keep your archive going.
